This petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, has been filed on behalf of petitioners assailing the impugned order dated 13.02.2024 passed by ASJ on an application filed by complainant seeking cancellation of bail in FIR No. 148/2020 registered at P.S. Mandir Marg for the offences punishable under Sections 420/468/471/120B IPC.
2.
Petitioners, namely, Braham Kumar Tanwar and Hrishikesh Kaushik have been granted bail vide order dated 01.08.2023.
It is apparent from the bail order that it was premised upon settlement which has been agreed between complainant and accused.

Settlement is contained in the statements Braham Kumar Tanwar vs The State on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160733767/
1 that were made in court, where no objections were given to the bail while being granted, in view of the settlement amount tendered through demand draft/cheques by the said accused persons.

Bail order was further granted on furnishing personal bond with the sum of Rs.50,000/- with one surety of the like amount and another depositing Rs.1,50,000/- in the name of the court, which was deposited in Court through demand draft.

It transpires that as regards the settlement amount while demand draft for Rs.1,50,000/- and Rs.2,50,000/- was presented for encashment, post-dated cheques dated 20.10.2022, 20.11.2022 and 20.02.2023 amounting to a total of Rs.3,50,000/- and another set of five post-dated cheques dated 20.09.2022, 20.11.2022, 20.12.2022, 20.01.2023 and 20.02.2022 amounting to Rs.7,90,000/- drawn by the wife of the accused Hrishikesh Kaushik were dishonoured.
4. Plea of learned counsel for petitioners that rely on the principles of cancellation of bail have been perused, however, the issue is slightly different in this matter.
5. Bail was premised upon no objection given by complainant to grant of bail on account of the settlement being arrived at.

6. Considering that the settlement itself was not honoured and in fact, cheques tendered by way of settlement were dishonoured, it prima facie shows that there was a deliberate attempt to deceive the complainant to procure bail.
The basic foundation on which the bail was granted collapses.

Ex-facie,
I do not find any infirmity in the impugned order.
7. Both accused are present in Court and seek another opportunity to pay the said amount to honour the settlement.

8. Considering the conduct of accused persons, the Court is wary of granting them another opportunity but in interest of justice, final opportunity is granted to them to pay said amount for which said cheques were dishonoured, within a period of six weeks.

9. It is made clear that if there is any violation of this undertaking, strict This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/07/2024 at 03:48:33 action would be taken against petitioners on the next date of hearing.
The said amounts will be paid through a demand draft on or before the next date of hearing.

Considering the statements made above, the amount of Rs.3,50,000/- that forms part of the settlement on the basis of which, no objection was given to the bail of petitioner Braham Kumar Tanwar and therefore, he will be responsible for tendering this amount; Hrishikesh Kaushik would tender an amount of Rs.7,90,000/- that form part of settlement on the basis of which, no objection was given for his bail and he shall be responsible for tendering this amount.
12. Both accused are directed to remain present in person, on the next date of hearing.
13.
At request of learned counsel for accused persons, no manner of any extension or mercy will be given on any ground.
14. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J JULY 12, 2024/ssc
